title: Baby Sound Explorers
strapline: Rattle, ring, crinkle, boom — a baby discovering that they can make sound happen.
intent: Babies discover cause and effect through sound: I shake it, it rattles; I bang it, it booms.
Babies experience a rich variety of sounds and textures, feeding early sensory and brain development.
Babies develop reaching, grasping, banging and shaking — the movements that make the sounds.
Babies begin to anticipate and repeat actions to hear a sound again, an early sign of intention.
Babies share the delight of making sounds with a warm, responsive adult who joins in.
implementation: Offer safe sound-makers — rattles, bells, shakers, crinkle toys, wooden blocks to knock together.
Include a treasure basket of natural sound-makers: a metal spoon and tin, a pine cone in a pot, a bunch of keys.
Follow the baby's lead — let them shake, mouth, bang and pause as long as they like.
Respond to each sound with delight: 'you made it ring!' so the baby connects action to effect.
Sit close and copy the baby's sounds back, turning it into a musical conversation.
Add a low sound wall or hanging metal objects to bat and swipe at.
Keep sounds gentle and check all objects are larger than a choke-tester and safe to mouth.
key_questions: Can you make it happen again?
Do you like the ring, or the crinkle?
What does this one sound like?

impact.text: Babies discover that their action makes a sound.
Babies repeat an action to make the sound happen again.
Babies reach, grasp, shake and bang with growing control.
Babies respond to sounds with stilling, movement and delight.
Babies share sound-making with an adult, taking turns.

enhancements: A low sound wall of pots, tins and metal tubes to bang.
Hanging metal objects and wind chimes to swipe and set ringing.
Treasure baskets of natural sound-makers to mouth and shake.
Crinkle books and fabrics for quieter sounds.
Different surfaces to bang a wooden spoon on — wood, metal, cushion.
Songs and gentle music to move and vocalise along with.

playing_exploring: Babies explore sound-makers freely with hands and mouth.
They test what each object does and how it sounds.
active_learning: Babies repeat an action many times to hear the sound again.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to expect the sound, connecting their action to the effect.
